item_1765032653875.label: Request Cribl.Cloud Org
item_1765032653875.title: Requesting A Cribl.Cloud Organization [CUSTOMER]
item_1765032653875.content:
Two business days before our POV kick-off, the customer should request a Cribl Cloud organization for the POV.

To request a Cribl.Cloud organization, follow these steps:
1. **Sign Up:** Go to https://cribl.cloud/signup/ and register using your work email address.
2. **Verify Account:** Use the verification code sent via email to confirm your registration.
3. **Create Organization:**
- On the **Create Organization** page, optionally enter an **Organization Name**.
- Select an AWS Region to host your Cribl.Cloud Leader.  Supported regions include:
  - US West (Oregon)
  - US East (Virginia)
  - US East (Ohio)
  - Europe (Frankfurt)
  - Europe (London)
  - Asia Pacific (Sydney)
  - Canada (Central)
- Click **Create Organization**.
4. **Access Organiztion:** Once the setup is complete, access your new Cribl.Cloud organization.

For more details visit the [Cribl.Cloud Initial Setup documentation](http://docs.cribl.io/stream/cloud-initial-setup/)

item_1765040147287.label: Invite Cribl SE to Cribl.Cloud Org
item_1765040147287.title: Invite the Cribl Solutions Engineer (SE) to your Cribl.Cloud organization as an Admin [CUSTOMER]
item_1765040147287.content:
Inviting the SE as an Admin allows them to upgrade the environment to an Enterprise Cloud Organization.  Optionally, this allows the SE to complete work outside of POV sessions.  This helps to alleviate some of the effort from the customer and expedite completion of the POV.

To invite someone to a Cribl.Cloud organization as an admin, follow these steps.

1. **Navigate to Members & Teams:**
- On the top bar, select **Products**, then **Cribl**.
- In the sidebar, go to **Organizations > Members & Teams**.
2. **Invite a Member:**
- Under the **Members** submenu, click **Invite Member**.
3. **Enter Details:**
- Provide the **Email** of the person you want to invite. ([SE_EMAIL_HERE])
- Optionally, add their **First Name** and **Last Name**. ([SE_NAME_HERE])
4. **Assign Permissions:**
- Under **Permissions**, select the **Admin** role to grant administrative access.
5. **Send the Invitation:**
- Click **Send Invite** to email the invitation.

The invited person will receive an email with a link to accept the invitation and join the organization.

For more details, visit the [Managing Cribl.Cloud Members documentation](docs.cribl.io/iam/permissions/)

item_1765147098771.label: Syslog
item_1765147098771.title: Configure Syslog Source in Cribl [CUSTOMER & CRIBL]
item_1765147098771.content:
**No TLS Method:**
- [ ] Create a new Syslog source: **Data > Sources > Syslog > Add Source**
- [ ] Provide a relevant name for your Source: eg. PaloAlto_Syslog
- [ ] Default port for **UDP** or **TCP** is **9514**
- [ ] Click **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**

**TLS method:**
- [ ] Clone existing **in_syslog_tls** source under **Data > Sources > Syslog**
- [ ] Open **in_syslog_tls**, click **Clone Source** at the bottom.
- [ ] Provide a relevant name for your Source: eg. PaloAlto_Syslog_tls
- [ ] Default port is **TCP 6514**
- [ ] Verify TLS Settings:
  - Enabled
  - **Private key path**: $CRIBL_CLOUD_KEY
  - **Certificate path**: $CRIBL_CLOUD_CRT
  - **Minimum TLS version**: TLSv1.2
- [ ] Click **Save**, then **Commit & Deploy**

For more details, refer to [Syslog Source Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/edge/sources-syslog/).

item_1765316616468.label: Panorama or Strata (Syslog)
item_1765316616468.title: Configure Panorama or Strata (Syslog) to send to Cribl [CUSTOMER]
item_1765316616468.content:
*TLS method:*
- [ ] Obtain the FQDN and port from your Cribl Cloud org.
- To find the FQDN and port, navigate to **Products > Cribl**
- On the left menu, under **Workspace**, select **Data Sources**.
- Scroll down until you see **in_syslog** in the **Name** field.  
- You can find your FQDN and port for UDP or TCP in the format: **default.main.<OrganizationID>.cribl.cloud:6514**

- [ ] Obtain the required certificates (**GTS Root R1** and **WR1**) from the **Google Trust Service Root Repository** [here](https://pki.goog/repository)
- **GTS Root R1** is under Root CAs
- **WR1** is under Subordinate CAs
- [ ] Import the certificates into PAN.  Mark each as a Trusted Root CA.
- [ ] Configure your firewall(s) to send syslog to the FQDN.  Be sure that there is nothing blocking data from being sent to port 6514.

item_1765752370674.label: Splunk Forwarder
item_1765752370674.title: Configure Splunk Forwarder to send to Cribl Stream [CUSTOMER]
item_1765752370674.content:
- [ ] Locate or create $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/system/local/outputs.conf.
- [ ] Edit outputs.conf and add an output group pointing at your Cribl Stream worker nodes (or URL if Cribl.Cloud).
**Send all logs from forwarder to Cribl Stream**

`**outputs.conf**`
`[tcpout]`
`defaultGroup=splunk,cribl`

`[tcpout:splunk]`
`server=10.1.1.197:9997, 10.1.1.198:9997`
`blockOnCloning=false`

`[tcpout:cribl]`
`server=10.1.1.200:9997, 10.1.1.199:9997`
`sendCookedData=true`

**Selectively send logs from forwarder to Cribl Stream**

`**outputs.conf**`
`[tcpout]`
`defaultGroup=splunk,cribl`

`[tcpout:splunk]`
`server=10.1.1.197:9997, 10.1.1.198:9997`
`blockOnCloning=false`

`[tcpout:cribl]`
`server=10.1.1.200:9997, 10.1.1.199:9997`
`sendCookedData=true`

`**inputs.conf**`
`# datasource1.log only gets sent to Splunk`
`[monitor:/path/to/log/datasource1.log]`
`_TCP_ROUTING = splunk`
`index = ds1_index`
`sourcetype = sourcetype1`

`# datasource2.log will get sent to both Splunk and Cribl Stream`
`[monitor:/path/to/log/datasource2.log]`
`_TCP_ROUTING = splunk, cribl`
`index = ds2_index`
`sourcetype = sourcetype2`

- [ ] Save, then bounce the forwarder.

item_1765913670681.label: Sentinel (Prepare Azure Workspace)
item_1765913670681.title: Prepare the Azure Workspace [CUSTOMER]
item_1765913670681.content:
[Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/usecase-azure-workspace/#prepare-the-azure-workspace)
It is helpful to walk through this together so we can ensure that the required pieces of information are captured in order to configure the Cribl Sentinel destination.

***Create Credentials for a New Azure Application***
[Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/usecase-azure-workspace/#create-credentials-for-a-new-azure-application)

- [ ] Log into **Azure portal** as an **Administrator**
- [ ] Go to **App registration** section.
- [ ] **New registration** to register an application.
- [ ] Register new application named **Cribl Stream**
- [ ] Click **Register**
- [ ] **!!** Store **Application (client) ID** and **Directory (tenant) ID** for later.
- [ ] In your newly registered app, select **Certificates & secrets** tab.
- [ ] Create a **New client secret**.
- [ ] **!!** Store the secret **Value** for later steps.

***Create a Data Collection Endpoint***
[Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/usecase-azure-workspace/#endpoint)

- [ ] Navigate to Azure portal’s **Monitor** service.
- [ ] Under **Settings**, select **Data Collection Endpoints**.
- [ ] Select **Create** to add a new endpoint named **Cribl-Stream-Ingestion**.
- [ ] Select appropriate **Subscription** and **Resource Group** used by your organization.
- [ ] Select **Review + create**, review your changes, then select **Create**.
- [ ] In the list of **Data Collection Endpoints**, open the new endpoint (you may need a page refresh).
- [ ] **!!** Navigate to **Overview** page and copy and store the **Logs Ingestion URL**.
- [ ] **!!** Select **JSON view** and store the value of the **Resource ID** (gray box at the top) for later use.

***Find the Log Analytics Workspace Resource ID***
[Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/usecase-azure-workspace/#find-the-log-analytics-workspace-resource-id)

- [ ] Navigate to Azure portal’s **Log Analytics workspaces** service.
- [ ] Select the workspace that will receive data.
- [ ] **!!** From the **Overview** page, select **JSON view** and store the value of the **Resource ID** (gray box at the top ) for later use.

***Create Data Collection Rule***

item_1765935176719.label: S3 Bucket
item_1765935176719.title: Configure AWS S3 Bucket for Cribl Stream Destination [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1765935176719.content:
***Step 1: Create the Amazon S3 Bucket***
- [ ] Log in to the **AWS Management Console** and navigate to the **S3** service.
- [ ] Click **Create bucket**.
- [ ] **Bucket name**: Enter a unique, globally non-generic name (e.g., cribl-logs-archive-12345).
- [ ] **AWS Region**: Select the region where you want to store the data. Note this for your Cribl Stream Destination configuration.
- [ ] Leave other settings as default (e.g., "Block all public access" should remain enabled).
- [ ] Click **Create bucket** and copy the **Bucket ARN** from the **Properties** tab for the next step.

***Step 2: Create IAM Policy for S3 Permissions***
- [ ] Navigate to the **IAM** service and select Policies.
- [ ] Click **Create Policy**.
- [ ] Switch to the **JSON** tab and paste the following permissions, replacing **<BUCKET_NAME>** with your name from Step 1:
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "s3:PutObject",
        "s3:ListBucket",
        "s3:GetBucketLocation"
      ],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:s3:::<BUCKET_NAME>",
        "arn:aws:s3:::<BUCKET_NAME>/*"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
- **Note**: **s3:ListBucket** and **s3:GetBucketLocation** are required for the bucket resource itself, while **s3:PutObject** is required for the objects within the bucket (/*).
- [ ] Click **Next**, then **Review**.
- [ ] **Name**: Enter a descriptive name (e.g., CriblStream_S3_Write_Policy).
- [ ] Click **Create policy**.

***Step 3: Create IAM Role with Trust Relationship (Assume Role)***
This step establishes a secure cross-account trust for the Cribl Stream Worker to assume this role.
- [ ] Navigate to **IAM** and select **Roles**.
- [ ] Click **Create role**.
- [ ] **Trusted entity type**: Select **Custom trust policy**.
- [ ] **Custom trust policy**: Paste the following JSON, ensuring you update the **Account ID**, **Role Name**, and **ExternalID** to match your environment:
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {
        "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/main-default"
      },
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
      "Condition": {
        "StringEquals": {
          "sts:ExternalId": "cribl-s3cre3t"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
- **Note**: You can find the **ARN** for your cloud worker group by going to **Products > Workspace**, then click **Access**.  Copy the value in the Trust field on the right side.
- [ ] Click **Next**.
- [ ] **Add Permissions**: Search for and attach the **IAM policy** created in Step 2 (e.g., CriblStream_S3_Write_Policy).
- [ ] Click **Next**.
- [ ] **Role name**: Enter a name (e.g., CriblStream_S3_Destination_Role).
- [ ] Click **Create role**.
- [ ] Open the newly created role and copy the **Role ARN**. You will need this for the **AssumeRole ARN** field in your Cribl Stream Destination settings.

For more details, refer to the [Amazon S3 Compatible Stores Destination Documentation](https://docs.cribl.io/stream/destinations-s3).

item_1769197445356.label: On-prem Leader Node
item_1769197445356.title: Deploy on-prem Leader Node (Linux) [CUSTOMER & CRIBL]
item_1769197445356.content:
***Minumum Recommended Specs***
TABLE:
Spec, Minimum Recommended (Can go smaller for POV)
OS, Linux: RH; CentOS; Ubuntu; AWS Linux (64bit)
Git, 1.8.3.1 or higher
CPU, 4 physical/8 vCPU
Memory, +8GB RAM
Disk, 5GB

***Prerequisites & System Prep***
- [ ] **Verify System Resources**
  - Ensure the instance meets the minimum requirements (e.g., 4 vCPUs / 8 GB RAM for a medium Leader).
- [ ] **Install Git**
  - Run `sudo yum install git` (Amazon Linux/RHEL) or `sudo apt-get install git` (Ubuntu/Debian). *Note: Required for Cribl's version control (Git) integration.*
- [ ] **Open Necessary Network Ports**
  - Port `9000`: Web UI/API access.
  - Port `4200`: Communication from Worker Nodes (heartbeat).
- [ ] **Create Dedicated Service User**
  - Create a `cribl` user to avoid running the service as root:
```
sudo useradd -m cribl
```

***Installation Steps***
- [ ] **Download the Cribl Binary**
  - Navigate to your install directory: `cd /opt`
  - Download the latest package: `curl -Lso cribl.tgz https://cdn.cribl.io/dl/latest`
- [ ] **Extract and Set Permissions**
  - Extract the archive: 
```
sudo tar -zxvf cribl.tgz
```
  - Change ownership: 
```
sudo chown -R cribl:cribl /opt/cribl
```
- [ ] **Start the Service Manually (Initial Run)**
  - Switch to the service user: 
```
sudo su - cribl
```
  - Start Cribl: 
```
/opt/cribl/bin/cribl start
```
- [ ] **Access the Web UI**
  - Navigate to `http://<YOUR_INSTANCE_IP>:9000`.
  - Log in with default credentials (`admin`/`admin`) and set a new password.

***Post-Install Configuration***
- [ ] **Enable Distributed Leader Mode**
  - Navigate to **Settings > Global Settings > Distributed Settings**.
  - Set **General Settings > Mode** to `Leader`.
  - Configure the **Address** (the IP or Hostname Workers will use to reach this Leader).
  - Click **Save** and then **Commit & Deploy**.

item_1777299264060.label: Direct Access - Splunk Cloud Self Storage (DDSS)
item_1777299264060.title: Configuring Direct Access in Lake for Splunk Cloud Self Storage (DDSS)
item_1777299264060.content:
***Splunk Cloud Self Storage (DDSS) Direct Access Checklist***

- [ ] Get your **Splunk Cloud ID**
  - In Splunk Cloud, navigate to **Settings > Storage** to find and copy your unique identifier.
- [ ] Create a **Cribl Lake Source**
  - In Cribl Lake, select **Direct Access** from the sidebar.
  - Select **Splunk Cloud Self Storage** and click **Next**.
  - Paste your **Splunk Cloud ID** into the designated field and click **Save**.
- [ ] Connect **Splunk Cloud** to the **Cribl Lake Storage Location**
  - Copy the **Amazon S3 bucket name** provided in the Cribl Lake UI.
  - In Splunk Cloud, go to **Settings > Storage > Self Storage Locations** and click **New Self Storage Location**.
  - Paste the bucket name and select **Generate** to create a bucket policy.
- [ ] Provision your **Cribl Lake**
  - Copy the generated bucket policy from Splunk Cloud.
  - Return to the Cribl Lake UI and paste the policy into the **Bucket Policy** field to authorize Splunk.
- [ ] Test and Submit the connection
  - In Splunk Cloud, click **Test** to allow Splunk to write a 0 KB validation file to Cribl Lake.
  - If the test is successful, click **Submit** to finalize the link.
- [ ] Create a **Cribl Lake Dataset**
  - In Cribl Lake, navigate to **Datasets > Add New**.
  - Ensure the **Dataset ID** exactly matches your **Splunk Index** name.
  - Set the **Data Format** to `DDSS`.
  - Set the **Storage Location** to the default `Cribl Lake`.

***Breaking a Direct Access Connection***

- [ ] Deleting a **Splunk Cloud Self Storage Source** (Cribl side):
  - Result: All Splunk data archived in Cribl Lake is lost.
  - Result: Splunk Cloud can no longer write to Cribl Lake.
  - *Note: Data flow within Splunk Cloud itself remains unaffected.*
- [ ] Deleting a **Self Storage Location** (Splunk side):
  - Result: Splunk stops archiving new data to Cribl Lake.
  - *Note: Existing data already stored in Cribl Lake remains intact.*
- [ ] Canceling **Splunk Cloud Account**:
  - Result: No new data can be written.
  - Result: Cribl Stream and Search can still read existing Dataset contents.

***Limitations of Splunk Cloud Direct Access***

- [ ] **Read-Only**: Datasets populated via Direct Access are read-only; Cribl Stream/Search cannot write to them.
- [ ] **Storage Location**: Must use the default `Cribl Lake` storage; external buckets are not supported.
- [ ] **Lakehouse**: Direct Access Datasets cannot be assigned to a Lakehouse.

***Troubleshooting Direct Access***

- [ ] If the Splunk **Test** fails, verify the following (corrections require re-creating the integration):
  - **Region Mismatch**: Ensure Splunk Cloud and Cribl.Cloud are in the same AWS region.
  - **Naming Schema**: Confirm the bucket name starts with your **Splunk Cloud ID**.
  - **Policy Accuracy**: Ensure the **Amazon S3 bucket policy** was copied and pasted exactly as generated.

***Configuration Parameters Summary***

TABLE: 
Parameter,Value/Requirement,Notes
Dataset ID,Matches Splunk Index,CRITICAL: Must match for search/replay to work
Data Format,`DDSS`,Required for Splunk journal file compatibility
Storage Location,`Cribl Lake`,Direct Access requires Cribl-managed storage
Splunk Cloud ID,Found in Splunk Settings,Uniquely identifies your cloud stack

item_1780671814476.label: Datadog
item_1780671814476.title: Configuring Datadog Destination in Cribl Stream [CUSTOMER + CRIBL]
item_1780671814476.content:
- [ ] In **Cribl Stream**, navigate to **Data > Destinations**.
- [ ] Select **Datadog** and click **Add Destination**.
- [ ] Fill in the required fields:
- **Output ID**: Provide a unique name for the destination.
- **Authentication Method**:** select Manual to enter an API key.
- **API Key**: Enter your Datadog organization's API key.
- **Datadog site**: Select the Datadog region your are sending to.  Defaults to US.
- **Send logs as**: specify how event payloads are delivered:
  - `application/json` (Default: structured JSON objects)
  - `text/plain` (Newline `\n` delimited raw strings)
- **Message field**: with the exact field name hosting your core payload. Leaving it blank defaults to sending the entire JSON object.  Set to **_raw**.
- **Datadog tags**: List of tags to send with logs. (e.g., `env:prod,app:billing`).
- [ ] Click **Save** then **Commit and Deploy**.

item_1781127766513.label: CrowdStrike FDR
item_1781127766513.title: Configuring the CrowdStrike FDR Source in Stream [CUSTOMER & CRIBL]
item_1781127766513.content:
***Prerequisites (Obtain from CrowdStrike Admin)***
- [ ] Secure the **FDR Credentials** and parameters needed for data retrieval:
  - AWS Access Key
  - AWS Secret Key
  - SQS Queue URL (or Name/ARN)
  - AWS Region (where the S3 bucket and SQS queue reside)

***Configure the CrowdStrike FDR Source in Cribl Stream***
- [ ] Navigate to **Data > Sources** in **Cribl Stream**.
- [ ] Select **CrowdStrike FDR** and click **Add Source**.
- [ ] Fill in the ***General Settings*** fields:
  - **Input ID**: Provide a unique name for the source (e.g., CrowdStrike_FDR_logs).
  - **Queue**: The name, URL, or ARN of the SQS queue to read notifications from. (e.g., 'https://host:port/myQueueName').
- [ ] Configure the ***Optional Settings*** panel:
  - Set the appropriate **Region** matching the bucket and queue location if it is not explicitly built into the Queue URL.
- [ ] Configure the ***Authentication*** panel:
  - Select **Manual** authentication.
  - Paste your CrowdStrike-provided AWS **Access key** and **Secret key** into their respective text boxes.
